Although in the proceedings so far, the fact of Mr. Zaric's appointment as chief for national security in Bosanski Samac has been explained to a significant degree, the Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric never actually took his duty upon himself, that this service was never established in Bosanski Samac, nor did it ever begin to function. The position that Mr. Zaric had, and the duties that he performed in Odzak, as assistant of the president of the civilian military council for security issues, was never disputed by Mr. Zaric's Defence. The Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric, in carrying out these duties, did not receive instructions, nor did he submit reports to the Crisis Staff of the Samac municipality. By presenting concrete evidence, the Defence will show that Mr. Zaric, in Odzak, just as he did before that in Bosanski Samac, carried out security and intelligence tasks comprising the gathering of information of significance for security and that in the performance of those tasks, he reported exclusively to the military authorities in Odzak, to whom he sent reports about his activities. Mr. Zaric's Defence will prove that between April and July 1992, he did not, together with Mr. Miroslav Tadic, work on organising exchanges. In that time period, Mr. Zaric was engaged on compiling lists of Serbs detained in the territory of the municipality of Odzak, solely because he is from the village of Trnjak-Zorice, which is in the territory of the municipality of Odzak, and thus he knew practically all of the villagers from his village. The list of captured Serbs in the compilation of which Mr. Zaric participated was given to representatives of the Red Cross of the municipality of Bosanski Samac and the activities of Mr. Zaric ended at this point. Mr. Zaric at no time denied that on a couple of occasions he talked with representatives of Odzak by radio at the communication centre of the municipality of Bosanski Samac. The Defence will prove that these conversations took place upon the insistence of the Odzak side and that on that occasion, representatives from Odzak insisted that they wanted to speak with Mr. Zaric himself. The purpose of those conversations and all of the activity of Mr. Zaric was aimed at facilitating contacts between representatives of the municipality of Odzak with a detained priest, Father Jozo Puskaric. The case so far has already indicated that since the end of May 1992, Mr. Zaric did not have any contacts with representatives of Odzak, which the Defence will prove by presenting additional evidence. The Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric did not achieve any kind of agreement with Odzak representatives and that their last contact ended in threats and insults addressed to Mr. Zaric. Mr. Zaric never acted together with Mr. Simic and Mr. Tadic, nor any other person, in planning, instigating, ordering, committing, or otherwise aiding and abetting the planning, preparation, or execution of the unlawful deportation and forcible transfer of the population, based on political, racial, or religious convictions. Evidence so far clearly shows that Mr. Zaric knew Mr. Simic slightly, superficially, that they did not share the same political views, and that they did not have any direct contact before the war; that Zaric never visited Mr. Simic in his apartment, or vice versa. Mr. Zaric did not have any particular contact with Mr. Tadic either, except for the fact that both of them were members of the 4th Detachment and that Mr. Zaric went to the AS cafe on several occasions. Mr. Tadic never went to Mr. Zaric's apartment, and Mr. Zaric, perhaps once or twice, went to Mr. Tadic's apartment during all the years that they have known each other. The Defence of Mr. Zaric will prove that there was no joint enterprise between Mr. Zaric and any other person in the persecution of non-Serb population in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Facts indicate, without a doubt, that when we are talking about Mr. Zaric, that would practically mean participation in the expulsion of a large part of his own family, which, for the most part, is not of Serb ethnicity. Neither Mr. Zaric nor the 4th Detachment participated in the forcible takeover of power by Serb forces in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, and the Defence will prove this fact by presenting numerous evidence. Based on evidence presented so far, it is clear that the key facilities in the municipality were taken over in the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, 1992. The 4th Detachment did not receive any order by the Superior Command to carry out any activities in the town, nor was such an order issued by the commander of the detachment. Members of the 4th Detachment spent that night in the same way as the majority of the citizens of Bosanski Samac: In their houses, on which there are numerous testimonies by Prosecution witnesses. Only during the day of the 17th of April did the 4th Detachment receive an order from the command of the 17th Tactical Group to take defensive positions on the outskirts of the town, on the banks of the Sava and Bosna Rivers, with the aim of preventing an attack by the Croatian army from the Republic of Croatia and units of the Croatian Defence Council from the direction of the Prud and Odzak villages. This order, which was implemented by members of the 4th Detachment, cannot be considered forcible takeover of power in the municipality and was of an exclusively defensive nature in preventing the attack against Bosanski Samac which followed soon after. The Defence will particularly again emphasise the position and the duties that Mr. Zaric had in the 4th Detachment, as well as the fact that he did not have any command authority. In addition to the order to take defence positions, the 4th Detachment received an order to collect illegal military weapons from the citizens who had them in their possession. The Defence will prove that in implementing this order, Mr. Zaric did not take part as a person directly involved but, rather, under the orders of the commander, he supervised how this order was being implemented. In connection with this fact, Mr. Zaric's Defence will bring witnesses who were directly involved and who were eyewitnesses of these events. Count 15(b) of the fifth amended indictment, Mr. Zaric is charged with taking part in unlawful arrests and detention of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims and other non-Serbian civilians on political, religious, or racial grounds and not for the purpose of their protection and security. The Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric was not in any way involved in the arrest and detention of non-Serbian population in Bosanski Samac. The evidence presented so far clearly indicate that neither Mr. Zaric nor any other member of the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army arrested a single individual or had such powers. On the contrary, all the witnesses who were heard and who themselves had been arrested and detained stated that they had been arrested either by members of paramilitary forces, the so-called Sareni, or camouflaged, or members of the Serbian police of the public security station in Bosanski Samac. The witnesses that Mr. Zaric's Defence intends to call will corroborate this fact, and it will prove that the only person who was authorised and who made decisions on which persons were going to be arrested and detained was chief of the public security station in Bosanski Samac, Stevan Todorovic. Stevan Todorovic was the only one who decided which individuals would be released from the police station, the TO staff, or any other location in which they were detained. For that purpose, the Defence will bring witnesses who themselves had been detained by the Serbian police. Also, Mr. Zaric's Defence will prove that all the individuals who had been detained during the war in Bosanski Samac were in custody of the Serbian police, that all the guards who guarded the detainees in the public security station, the Territorial Defence building, or in the high school, were members of the Serbian police and that the Serbian police was responsible for the security of detainees. In proving these facts, the Defence will primarily rely on the testimonies by witnesses who at the time were members of the Serbian police and who have direct knowledge of all these facts. Mr. Zaric's Defence has never disputed the fact that the individuals detained in the public security station, the Territorial Defence building, and the high school were subjected to beating, torture, and that they were kept in inhumane conditions. What Mr. Zaric's Defence will prove in arguing its case is that Mr. Zaric had never, in any way, took part in the beatings or torturing of detainees or that he exerted any influence on the conditions in which they were kept. Not only that; the Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric publicly condemned these phenomena and did everything within his ability to remove the detainees and spare them the beating and the torture. A variety of evidence of this kind of conduct of Mr. Zaric have been presented during the presentation of the case by the Prosecutor. Let us just recall at this time the testimony given by Sulejman Tihic, Ibrahim Salkic, the Witness N, and others. Further, the Defence will prove that at the time when the torturing and the beating up of the detainees was at its peak, when one of the detainees was murdered, Mr. Zaric initiated and organised a transfer of a large group of detainees to the military barracks in Brcko, and thereby most definitely saved many lives that were in danger. The witnesses for the Prosecution who spoke about this pointed out, without exception, that the conditions in the Detention Unit in Brcko were incomparably better than those in Bosanski Samac, that they were not beaten up, and that they were allowed to take a bath and to receive medical treatment. The Defence will prove that this action of Mr. Zaric was motivated exclusively by reasons of security and safety of detainees and the need to help them by placing them out of the reach of the Serbian police and the volunteers Also, the Defence will prove what kind of consequences were suffered by Mr. Zaric himself as a result of this act, to what kind of humiliation and threats he was exposed on account of this, and how he had to go into hiding because his life was threatened. The Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric had no connection whatsoever with what the Prosecutor calls forced labour and what the Defence refer to as the work obligation by using the formulation or the phrase from the laws then in force. It has become already clear and apparent that engaging individuals for work obligation was exclusively under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. In the course of presenting the case, Mr. Zaric's Defence will prove that Mr. Zaric was not in any way involved in that, nor did he have any influence on that. Regarding the charges that Mr. Zaric interviewed the detained Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and other non-Serbian civilians, and forced them to sign false statements made under duress, but without disputing the fact that Mr. Zaric did conduct interviews with a few detainees, the Defence will prove the following: Mr. Zaric conducted interviews with detainees on orders from his superior officers, with a view to gathering security information regarding the illegal arming, based on ethnic and party affiliations. Mr. Zaric had never resorted to force or threats while conducting interviews with the detainees. Everything that the detainees stated during these interviews, Mr. Zaric accurately translated into written statements. Mr. Zaric never forced anyone to sign a written statement. The content of these statements is identical to the one -- to what the Prosecution witnesses heard about the circumstances stated before this Tribunal. Mr. Zaric's Defence would like to underline once again that during the Prosecution case, all witnesses who made statements about these circumstances confirmed that the interviews they had with Mr. Zaric were conducted in a completely fair manner and without any threats or use of force. Mr. Zaric did not take part in any way whatsoever in forcible relocation and expulsion of the Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and other non-Serbian civilians, including women, children, and the elderly, from their homes and villages, by using force, intimidation, and coercion. The Defence will prove that by hearing witnesses who, during the hostilities in Bosanski Samac, abandoned their homes. These witnesses will explain their reasons for abandoning their homes, but also the fact that none of the actions of Mr. Zaric was related to that in any way. Mr. Zaric's Defence will prove that in no way did he participate in plunder and seizure of the property of the Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and other non-Serbian civilians, including housing facilities, shops, personal belongings, and livestock, without disputing the fact that there were such incidents in the territory of Bosanski Samac and Odzak while the hostilities were in progress. The Defence will prove that as far back as in 1992, Mr. Zaric publicly pointed to these incidents and condemned it. The Defence will present evidence which will demonstrate what kind of efforts Mr. Zaric personally made in order to protect the property of non-Serbs from seizure and plunder. Mr. Zaric's Defence will particularly, during its entire case, will prove that there did not exist any discriminatory intent on the part of Mr. Zaric against non-Serbian population, by relying on the statements made by the proposed witnesses, but also on the facts that speak undoubtedly in favour of Mr. Zaric, as well as his family situation and his political, sport, and cultural engagement. Finally, Mr. Zaric's Defence will prove that in the period between the 17th of April until 31st of December, 1992, did not commit a crime of deportation as a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(D) of the Statute of this Tribunal, or unlawful deportation or relocation as grave breaches of the 1949 Geneva Conventions, punishable under Article 2(G) of the Statute. After presenting its case, Mr. Zaric and his counsels are convinced that this Honourable Trial Chamber will have had a true picture about the personality of Mr. Zaric and his efforts to remain consistent and true to his principles, even under the most difficult war conditions, and to help to anyone he could possibly help, regardless of to which ethnicity or religious group that individual belonged, but also to condemn and stand up against any injustice or crime, regardless of who the perpetrators are. Mr. Zaric has decided, after the Defence has presented its case, to take the witness stand himself before this Trial Chamber, believing that, by way of his testimony, he will contribute to establishing the truth. At the end, Mr. Zaric's Defence will return to what has been said at the beginning of this opening statement. Mr. Zaric has not come before this Tribunal in order to cast a reasonable doubt on the evidence presented by the Prosecution against him. He came here to tell the truth and to use it as an instrument to fight fabricated allegations against himself. Mr. Zaric is convinced that after hearing his Defence case, this Honourable Chamber will pass the only judgement that he himself, but also many other citizens of Bosanski Samac, have been awaiting with impatience, a judgement that Mr. Zaric is not guilty on any counts of the indictment. Such decision of this Honourable Tribunal will make it possible for Mr. Zaric to return to his family and his town with dignity.

utterances.text: How long do you think you still have to go? MR. DI FAZIO: [Microphone not activated] I'm going to do everything that I possibly can to finish -- I'm going to do everything that I possibly can to try and finish tomorrow, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because you've already got -- you've already gone quite a long way in terms of time. MR. DI FAZIO: I appreciate that, Your Honour. I will re-look again at my notes and I will see if I can cut it down wherever I possibly can. My earnest hopes and endeavours will be to finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. We shall adjourn and continue our proceedings tomorrow.
